CONFIRMED STILL PRESENT (2026-07-20, current HEAD 26e5553). handle_rename is now at handlers.rs:2362-2390 (drifted from the hint's 2271-2299, but byte-identical in substance): lines 2366-2368 still unconditionally `return true` (dynamic, no binding recorded) whenever `naming::is_dynamic_word(&args[0]) || is_dynamic_word(&args[1])` (naming.rs:891-893, unchanged: `word.contains('$') || word.contains('[')`), never calling resolve_const_word/lookup_const_string. None of this session's other landed fixes (923: namespace/class dynamic-target collisions, interp create/eval, qualified var lookup, param spans) touch handle_rename, is_dynamic_word, or rename_.rs — `git log -- handlers.rs naming.rs rename_.rs` shows no rename-specific commits. I built the existing binary (cargo test -p tcl-compiler --lib handle_rename: 10/10 pass, warm cache) and ran the packaged tcl-lsp-server (target/debug/tcl-lsp-server) via .claude/skills/lsp-client/lsp_client.py against fresh repros in the scratchpad, confirming end-to-end: `set old ::foo_impl; rename $old ::foo; puts [::foo]` and `set key impl; rename ::foo_$key ::foo` both give "Definition (0 locations)" / "(no hover)" today, while `rename ::foo_impl ::foo` (no vars) resolves correctly — exactly matching the finding. I also independently re-verified real-Tcl ground truth with both tclsh9.0 and tclsh8.6 (not just trusting the prior oracle_output): the renamed name really does run the original proc body and the old name is really gone.

THE FIX (two tiers; only Tier 1 is in scope for a "fix idx=3" ticket, Tier 2 is a much bigger, separate feature — see secondary_issues_found):

TIER 1 — constant-fold each rename argument before giving up, exactly as the root-cause hint prescribes, reusing existing infra:
1. Thread `arg_single: &[bool]` and `scope_path: &[usize]` into handle_rename (both already computed at the one call site, commands.rs:759-764 inside dispatch_analyser_hook, and already passed to sibling hooks like Hook::Set → handle_set_command two lines above at commands.rs:662) — handle_rename currently only takes `(args, arg_tokens, offset)` and has no way to consult the const-string lattice without them.
2. Replace the blanket `is_dynamic_word` bail-out with a per-argument resolver `resolve_rename_arg(text, tok, is_single, scope_path) -> Option<String>` that: (a) returns the word verbatim when `!is_dynamic_word(text)` (today's non-dynamic path, unchanged); (b) otherwise first tries the EXISTING `resolve_const_word` (handlers.rs:424-444) — this alone closes the finding's own simplest repro, `set old ::foo_impl; rename $old ::foo` (single whole-word Var token), and correctly respects Tcl's brace-suppresses-substitution rule for free (a `Str`-kind single token literally containing `$`/`[` text, e.g. `rename {::pkg::$c} ::pkg::foo`, is legitimately static and resolve_const_word already returns it as-is — is_dynamic_word alone would have wrongly flagged it dynamic); (c) if that fails and the word is NOT single-token (a concatenation like `::mypkg::${c}_$key`), fold it via a NEW small helper in text.rs (see below) fed by `self.lookup_const_string`.
3. New helper `fold_interpolation_single(word: &str, resolve_var: impl FnMut(&str) -> Option<String>) -> Option<String>` in rust/tcl-compiler/src/text.rs. This is the single-value analogue of the EXISTING `fold_interpolation_set` (text.rs:233-327, `pub(crate)`, same crate as analyser/handlers.rs so directly callable via `crate::text::...` — this exact cross-module call shape is already established, e.g. scope.rs:943 calls `crate::text::suggest_similar`). fold_interpolation_set already does 90% of what's needed (splits a reconstructed word like `${a}${b}` into literal/`$var` segments, rejects `[` command substitution, rejects array-indexed `$x(idx)`) but is wired for the SCCP `HashMap<String, HashSet<String>>` (multi-value ConstSet) lattice used by the *later*, CFG/SSA-dependent W123 diagnostics pass (var_command.rs:1390 resolve_interpolated_w123_diagnostics) — that lattice isn't built yet when handle_rename runs (single AST walk, pre-CFG/SSA). Recommended refactor: extract fold_interpolation_set's segment-scan loop into a shared `split_interpolation_segments(word) -> Option<Vec<Segment<'_>>>` (Segment::Literal(&str) | Segment::Var(&str)), then implement fold_interpolation_set in terms of it (Cartesian product, unchanged behavior/tests) and add fold_interpolation_single as a second, thin consumer that concatenates one resolved value per Var segment via the caller-supplied closure, short-circuiting to None on the first unresolvable variable or any `[`. This keeps exactly one word-interpolation parser in the codebase instead of two independent regexes of $/${} scanning logic.
4. In resolve_rename_arg's fallback, the closure is `|name| self.lookup_const_string(name, scope_path).map(str::to_string)` — scope.rs:522, the SAME lexical/straight-line ("last write wins", ancestor-scope-chain) lattice resolve_const_word and resolve_expansion_count (handlers.rs:3324, the literal precedent named in the root-cause hint) already use. No new lattice, no CFG/SSA dependency.
5. handle_rename then resolves both args via resolve_rename_arg; only `None`/`None` (still genuinely unresolvable, or a `[`-bearing word, or a missing token in the handful of hand-built unit tests that pass `arg_tokens: &[]`) falls through to today's `return true` (dynamic). On success it runs the EXISTING downstream logic (normalise_qualified_name, renamed_commands/rename_offsets/deleted_commands/rename_target_spans/result.renamed_commands) completely unchanged — I verified the representative `arg_tokens[i]`'s span already covers the WHOLE reconstructed word even for a multi-token word (segmenter.rs test `multi_token_word_argv_spans_full_word`), so `rename_target_spans`'s span bookkeeping needs no change.

Existing patterns explicitly checked per the task's list: `@interp@`/`@dynns@`/`@dynclass@` synthetic scope keys — not applicable (that machinery accepts a call site as genuinely dynamic and merges scopes; this fix instead proves more call sites are NOT dynamic). `leading_option_word_count` (tcl-registry/spec.rs) — N/A, rename has no leading options. `lookup_var_in_namespace` (scope.rs) — different purpose (qualified cross-namespace variable reads); the correct sibling is `lookup_const_string` in the same file. `offset_is_inside_any_definition_body` (types.rs) — not relevant to the fold, but IS the gate `resolve_called_proc` already uses, relevant to secondary issue #1 below.

proposed_changes.description: Add `arg_single: &[bool]` and `scope_path: &[usize]` parameters. Replace the `if is_dynamic_word(args[0]) || is_dynamic_word(args[1]) { return true; }` bail-out with two calls to a new `resolve_rename_arg` helper (one per argument); only bail dynamic when either call returns `None`. Feed the resolved (String, String) pair into the existing normalise_qualified_name/renamed_commands/deleted_commands/rename_target_spans logic unchanged. Also update the doc comment (currently says the handler 'returns true when dynamic ... rename $x y / rename x [y]') to describe the new constant-folding attempt.
proposed_changes.existing_pattern_to_reuse: resolve_const_word (handlers.rs:424-444) and lookup_const_string (scope.rs:522) — exactly the helpers resolve_expansion_count (handlers.rs:3324) already uses for the analogous `{*}$var`-with-known-value case, per the root-cause hint.

proposed_changes.function_or_area: new private fn resolve_rename_arg (place near resolve_const_word or directly above handle_rename)
proposed_changes.description: `fn resolve_rename_arg(&self, text: &str, tok: Option<&Token>, is_single: Option<&bool>, scope_path: &[usize]) -> Option<String>`. If `!is_dynamic_word(text)`, return `Some(text.to_string())` (today's behavior, zero cost). Else require a token (`tok?`), try `self.resolve_const_word(text, *tok, is_single, scope_path)` first (handles a pure single Var, and correctly leaves a braced literal like `{::pkg::$c}` alone since resolve_const_word inspects TokenType::Str vs Var). If that fails, call `crate::text::fold_interpolation_single(text, |name| self.lookup_const_string(name, scope_path).map(str::to_string))` for the multi-token concatenation case. Missing token (the handful of existing unit tests call handle_rename with `arg_tokens: &[]`) must fall through to None, not panic.
proposed_changes.existing_pattern_to_reuse: Mirrors resolve_const_word's own two-branch dispatch (handlers.rs:424-444); no new lattice.

proposed_changes.description: Extract the existing `$`/`${}` segment-scanning loop (currently inlined in fold_interpolation_set) into a shared `fn split_interpolation_segments(word: &str) -> Option<Vec<Segment<'_>>>` with `enum Segment<'a> { Literal(&'a str), Var(&'a str) }`, preserving today's exact rejection rules (empty word, any `[`, unterminated `${`, bare `$` not followed by an identifier char, `$name(` array-indexed reads). Reimplement fold_interpolation_set on top of it (Cartesian product over HashSet values — behavior-preserving, its existing tests must keep passing unchanged). Add `pub(crate) fn fold_interpolation_single(word: &str, resolve_var: impl FnMut(&str) -> Option<String>) -> Option<String>` that walks the same segments and string-concatenates, `?`-short-circuiting to None on the first Var the closure can't resolve.
proposed_changes.existing_pattern_to_reuse: fold_interpolation_set itself (text.rs:233), already pub(crate) and already cross-module-called from analyser/diagnostics/var_command.rs — same crate as analyser/handlers.rs, so `crate::text::fold_interpolation_single` needs no visibility changes.

proposed_changes.description: Change `self.handle_rename(args, arg_tokens, cmd_tok.span.start())` to `self.handle_rename(args, arg_tokens, arg_single, scope_path, cmd_tok.span.start())` — both `arg_single` and `scope_path` are already in scope as this function's own parameters (used two arms above by Hook::Set at line 662).

Mechanical signature migration only: add `&[]` (arg_single) and `&[]` (scope_path) to each existing call. I traced all 5 by hand against the proposed logic — every one still asserts the same outcome post-fix (the two 'dynamic' tests pass empty arg_tokens, so resolve_rename_arg's `tok?` guard correctly still returns None → still reported dynamic, unchanged).

proposed_changes.function_or_area: handle_foreach_command / define_vars_from_list (1729-1771) — OPTIONAL, separately scoped widening, see secondary_issues_found
proposed_changes.description: Track a `foreach VAR LIST body` loop variable as a constant (via set_const_string) when LIST is a literal (Str/Esc single-token) list with exactly one element. Safe and intraprocedural (exactly one write, dominates the whole body) but does NOT by itself close the tcllib json.tcl idiom (apicmds has 2 elements) — see secondary_issues_found for why this is necessary-but-not-sufficient.

proposed_changes.function_or_area: async fn hover (9957-10002) — SEPARATE, larger fix, see secondary_issues_found
proposed_changes.description: Add a cross-document fallback tier to hover, modeled on goto_definition's compute_definition → cross_document_definition (lib.rs:3633-3706) / autoload_definition (3717-3749) pattern: when core_hover::hover_with_profile returns None and the cursor is on a command head, consult self.workspace_index (resolve_command_target / proc_definitions_qualified) to chase rename/alias/import links to the defining document, analysis_for() that document, look up the ProcDef in its all_procs, and render via the existing proc_hover_text(). Needed because hover_with_profile / resolve_called_proc (tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs:1169) only ever consult analysis.all_procs directly and never analysis.renamed_commands — confirmed by grep (renamed_commands appears nowhere in tcl-lsp-core/src/hover.rs or definition.rs, only in workspace_index.rs) and by empirical test: hover on a call reached through even the fully-literal, always-worked `rename ::foo_impl ::foo` still prints '(no hover)' today, both same-file and cross-file.

AFTER TIER 1: definition/references resolve, via fold_interpolation_single splitting `::foo_$key` into Literal("::foo_") + Var("key") and resolving key=impl through lookup_const_string.

Two concatenated resolvable Vars in the SAME straight-line proc scope (the closest Tier-1-fixable approximation of the tcllib shape, deliberately without the foreach/parameter indirection that blocks the real idiom): `namespace eval ::mypkg {}` / `proc ::mypkg::greet_tcl {name} {return "hi $name"}` / `proc ::mypkg::activate {} {set c greet; set key tcl; rename ::mypkg::${c}_$key ::mypkg::${c}}` / `::mypkg::activate` / `puts [::mypkg::greet world]`. Expected after Tier 1: go-to-definition on `::mypkg::greet` resolves to greet_tcl's proc.

Cross-file, Tier-1-resolvable (proc, rename, and call site in three different files, matching the real idiom's file layout but with `set`-based c/key instead of foreach/parameter): impl.tcl defines `::foo_impl`; setup.tcl does `source impl.tcl; set key impl; rename ::foo_$key ::foo`; user.tcl does `source setup.tcl; puts [::foo]`. I directly verified the analogous ALREADY-WORKING literal-rename version of this exact 3-file shape resolves definition AND references correctly today via workspace_index's command_links/resolve_command_target/invocations_of (impl.tcl 0:5-0:15, setup.tcl 1:7-1:17, user.tcl 1:6-1:11 all reported) — so once handle_rename populates renamed_commands for this dynamic-but-resolvable case, the SAME already-working cross-file machinery should pick it up with no further change. Hover still needs the separate fix.

THE FINDING'S OWN HEADLINE SCENARIO — run this AFTER implementing Tier 1 ONLY and confirm it is EXPECTED to still fail (not a regression): greet_tcl.tcl defines `proc ::mypkg::greet_tcl {name} {...}`; mypkg.tcl has `proc ::mypkg::SwitchTo {key} { foreach c {greet} { rename ::mypkg::${c}_$key ::mypkg::${c} } }` called as `foreach e {tcl} { ::mypkg::LoadAccelerator $e; ::mypkg::SwitchTo $e }`; user.tcl calls `::mypkg::greet`. I built and ran this exact repro live (scratchpad/rename_repro/{mypkg.tcl,greet_tcl.tcl,user.tcl}): definition/hover both fail today. They will STILL fail after Tier 1 alone, because `key` is SwitchTo's bare PROC PARAMETER (never `set`, never in const_strings) and `c` is a `foreach`-loop variable (define_vars_from_list only calls define_var, never set_const_string) — neither is reachable via lookup_const_string. I also read the REAL tcllib source (tmp/tcllib-2.0/modules/json/json.tcl:26-98) and confirmed the actual json::SwitchTo has the identical shape (`proc ::json::SwitchTo {key} {... foreach c $apicmds { rename ::json::${c}_$key ::json::${c} } ...}`), so this is not an artifact of my simplified repro.

Isolated foreach-var-only gap (to test Tier-2a's optional foreach-single-literal-element widening in isolation, if implemented): `proc ::foo_impl {} {return impl}` / `foreach c {foo} { rename ::${c}_impl ::${c} }` / `puts [::foo]`. Expected: still FN after Tier 1 alone (c is a loop var, not const-tracked); becomes TP if the optional handle_foreach_command widening (proposed_changes item 6) is also implemented, since the list has exactly one element.

Isolated parameter-only gap, to document as explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: `proc ::foo_impl {} {return impl}` / `proc activate {key} { rename ::foo_$key ::foo }` / `activate impl` / `puts [::foo]`. Expected: still FN even with Tier 1 AND the foreach widening — closing this needs interprocedural single-call-site literal-argument propagation into the parameter, a materially larger and riskier feature; recommend scoping as a separate follow-up finding rather than silently expecting it here.

Genuinely dynamic value must remain unresolved (regression guard against over-eager folding): `proc ::foo_impl {} {...}` / `set old [gets stdin]` / `rename $old ::foo`. `gets` is never recorded in const_strings, so lookup_const_string returns None and handle_rename must still report dynamic=true / has_dynamic_providers=true, exactly as today.

Existing fully-literal rename (finding's own control check) must keep working byte-for-byte identically — this path never even enters the new resolver since is_dynamic_word is false for both args: `proc ::foo_impl {} {...}` / `rename ::foo_impl ::foo` / `puts [::foo]`. I verified this already resolves correctly today (definition: 1 location at the proc's declaration); must be unaffected.

Branch-imprecision / soundness-boundary case — add as a PINNED regression test documenting KNOWN behavior rather than asserting 'correctness', since it inherits an imprecision already accepted by resolve_const_word/resolve_expansion_count: `proc ::foo_implA {} {return A}` / `proc ::foo_implB {} {return B}` / `proc pick {cond} { if {$cond} {set key implA} else {set key implB}; rename ::foo_$key ::foo }` / `pick 1`. const_strings is documented as 'last-write-wins across if/loop joins' (scope.rs comment near lookup_const_string_with_span), so the analyser will likely bind ::foo to whichever branch it walked last (probably implB) regardless of the runtime `cond` value passed at the one call site. Not a new hole (pre-existing lattice limitation) but worth an explicit test so behavior is documented and doesn't silently worsen.

Bonus side-effect worth a dedicated regression test — W123 (unknown command) should stay USEFULLY active instead of being blanket-suppressed once a rename resolves statically: `proc ::foo_impl {} {...}` / `set key impl` / `rename ::foo_$key ::foo` / `totally_unknown_command_xyz`. TODAY: the misclassified 'dynamic' rename sets has_dynamic_providers=true, which unconditionally suppresses W123 for the WHOLE file (diagnostics/unresolved.rs:111-119) — so `totally_unknown_command_xyz` currently gets NO W123 diagnostic, a latent false negative caused by this same bug. AFTER Tier 1: the rename resolves statically, has_dynamic_providers stays false (from this construct), and W123 should fire on the genuinely-unknown command.

secondary_issues_found:
#1 (MOST IMPORTANT — scope/expectation mismatch): The root-cause-hinted fix (lexical lookup_const_string folding) will NOT by itself make the finding's own headline FAILURE SCENARIO start working. I built the exact mypkg.tcl/greet_tcl.tcl/user.tcl repro from the failure_scenario text, ran it live against the built server (confirming today's failure), and then traced the data flow by hand: in that repro (and in the REAL tcllib modules/json/json.tcl:61-93 SwitchTo, which I also read directly), the rename's two substituted names come from (a) `$c`, a `foreach c {...}` LOOP VARIABLE — handlers.rs's define_vars_from_list (1729-1743) only calls define_var, never set_const_string, so foreach vars are never in the const_strings lattice regardless of how literal the list is — and (b) `$key`, a bare PROC PARAMETER of SwitchTo — parameters are never `set`, so they're never in const_strings either, and resolving them would need genuine interprocedural (single-call-site literal-argument) propagation that doesn't exist anywhere pre-CFG/SSA. Neither is 'assigned earlier in the same straight-line scope' in the sense lookup_const_string actually supports. The finding's OWN simplest isolated repros (`set old ...; rename $old ::foo` and `set key impl; rename ::foo_$key ::foo`) ARE fully `set`-based and ARE fixed by Tier 1 — I verified both fail today and traced both resolving correctly post-fix — so Tier 1 is real, valuable, and matches what was literally asked, but the implementer/reviewer must not assume it closes the tcllib-idiom motivating example without also doing the foreach-widening (partial help) and/or the interprocedural parameter work (the real closer, and a materially bigger feature). I've proposed the foreach widening as an optional Tier-2a change and explicitly recommend treating full parameter propagation as a separate follow-up finding.

#2 (real, independently-confirmed, pre-existing bug, NOT caused by is_dynamic_word): Hover never resolves a call reached through ANY rename — including the fully-literal case the finding cites as proof 'the harness and rename machinery work in general'. tcl-lsp-core/src/hover.rs's hover_with_profile only special-cases interp alias (via alias_hover_text reading analysis.command_aliases); its proc-hover branch calls definition.rs's resolve_called_proc, which only ever searches analysis.all_procs — grep confirms `renamed_commands` appears nowhere in hover.rs or definition.rs, only in workspace_index.rs (consumed by goto_definition's cross-document fallback in lib.rs, and by references, but not by hover). I proved this empirically two ways: (a) same-file `rename ::foo_impl ::foo; puts [::foo]` — definition resolves (1 location) but hover on `::foo` prints '(no hover)'; (b) a clean 3-file version (impl.tcl/setup.tcl/user.tcl) — definition AND references both correctly resolve cross-file (via workspace_index), hover still prints '(no hover)'. This means even a 'perfect' Tier-1 fix leaves hover broken for the finding's stated goal ('go-to-definition and hover... return nothing'). Closing it needs a new cross-document hover fallback tier in lib.rs's `async fn hover`, mirroring goto_definition's existing cross_document_definition/autoload_definition pattern (both already read self.workspace_index and re-analyse a target document on demand) — this is a distinct, non-trivial, separately-scoped fix; I've sketched it in proposed_changes but it is materially bigger than the Tier-1 analyser change and touches async server code, not just tcl-compiler.

#3 (minor, same-file only, low priority): references on a same-file rename+call (all three of proc/rename/call in ONE document) found only the proc's own declaration span, missing both the rename statement's OLD-arg mention and the call site — even for the always-worked literal case. The cross-file version of the identical shape (proc, rename, call each in a different file) found all three correctly. This looks like `resolve_workspace_symbols`'s declaration-cursor branch (lib.rs ~3974-3983) returning only the cursor's own qualified name with no reverse chase through renamed_commands (old→which news alias it), masked in the cross-file case because cross_document_references' cross-file invocation search does the forward chase via command_links/follow_links correctly. Lower priority than #1/#2 since the real multi-file idiom is unaffected, but worth a look if the implementer is already touching this area.

#4 (non-issue, worth clarifying so it isn't 'fixed' by accident in a way that breaks something else): the finding's claim that 'symbols mypkg.tcl lists only Function greet_tcl (never greet)' is not obviously a bug — document symbols reflect physical proc declarations (name_span at the `proc` keyword); a `rename`-introduced alternate name has no declaration site of its own to point at, and the LSP doesn't synthesize one for `interp alias` targets either. I'd treat 'symbols' as out of scope for this fix unless the implementer specifically wants to design a synthetic outline entry for renamed-to names (a UX decision, not a resolution bug).

#5 (related, out-of-scope observation): `handle_interp_alias`'s cross-domain branch (handlers.rs:2282-2314) has the identical is_dynamic_word-only gate (via its local `literal` closure) with no constant-folding attempt either — plausibly the same class of bug for `interp alias`, but that's a different command/finding; flagging for awareness, not folding into this fix.

#6 (soundness note, not a blocker): const_strings is a lexical, 'last write wins across if/loop joins' lattice (per its own doc comment in scope.rs) — a rename whose variable is assigned differently on divergent if/else branches could resolve to a value that isn't actually guaranteed at the call site. This is a pre-existing, already-accepted imprecision shared by every other lookup_const_string consumer (resolve_const_word, resolve_expansion_count, handle_defines_symbol), not something newly introduced by this fix, but it's worth an explicit pinned test (included in test_scenarios) since rename's resolved value feeds go-to-definition/hover correctness (arguably higher-stakes than the cosmetic uses this lattice serves elsewhere).
open_questions: (1) Should this ticket's scope include the Tier-2a foreach-single-literal-element widening (handle_foreach_command / define_vars_from_list)? It's cheap and safe but only partially closes the real tcllib idiom (apicmds has 2 elements, so even with this widening `$c` would need multi-valued ConstSet tracking, not scalar lookup_const_string). (2) Should the hover cross-document gap (secondary issue #2) be fixed in the same PR/ticket, given the finding's SUMMARY explicitly promises hover, or filed as a separate follow-up given it touches lib.rs's async server layer rather than just tcl-compiler? (3) Is full interprocedural single-call-site parameter constant-propagation (closing secondary issue #1's `$key` half) wanted at all, or should the tcllib-idiom-specific case simply be accepted as a documented FN/limitation? This is a meaningfully larger feature (soundness questions: workspace-wide, multi-file, must stay correct as the user edits and adds a second call site) that I'd recommend NOT bundling into this fix. (4) For the branch-imprecision case (secondary issue #6), does the team want the pinned regression test to just document today's actual (whatever-it-is) behavior, or would they rather explicitly special-case rename to refuse folding across any conditional (a stricter, more conservative policy this fix's author could add as a deliberate carve-out — I did not design this since it's a genuinely new policy decision, not implied by existing precedent)?

approach_summary: Add one new, self-contained "straight-line value-flow" fact — `set VAR [interp create ?-safe? ?--? ?path?]` binds VAR to an interpreter-domain key — mirroring the *scope-chain-aware* shape of `const_strings`, not the flat shape of `instance_classes`. Populate it inside `handle_set_command` (handlers.rs:154), which already runs the same set/clear dance for constant strings, so the fix reuses that function's existing structure instead of adding a new dispatch path. Then teach the three existing dynamic-path consumers (`handle_interp_alias`'s cross-domain branch, `handle_interp_eval_command`'s dynamic-path branch, and `handle_interp_handle_eval_command`'s `cmd_name`) to resolve a plain `$VAR`/`${VAR}` word through this new binding before falling back to their current (literal-only, or raw-text-keyed) behaviour. Critically, when `interp create` has no literal path, key the recorded interpreter state by a synthetic *per-call-site* token (mirroring 26e5553's `@dynns@<offset>` / `@dynclass@<offset>`, e.g. `@autoname@<offset-of-the-[interp-create-...]-substitution>`), NOT by the variable's raw text — this is what makes the fix also close the newly-found cross-contamination hole (secondary issue #2) for the tracked subset, rather than reproducing it. No CFG/branch-sensitivity is needed or wanted: the hint explicitly frames this as straight-line, last-write-wins tracking, consistent with how `const_strings` itself already behaves.

secondary_issues_found:
Three related issues surfaced while reading the surrounding code and empirically probing it — all reproduced against the live tcl-lsp-server binary, none fixed by the two commits that landed earlier this session (37e6886, 26e5553):

1. (Directly blocks the real-world motivating case, not just the minimal repro) `handle_interp_handle_eval_command` (the `$VAR eval { ... }` object-command form) only ever resolves a LITERAL `cmd_name`; its own doc comment already states this is deliberate ("resolving a *variable's* interpreter value is the separate, harder value-flow problem ... not one this handler takes on"). doctools.tcl's actual SetupFormatter proc (tmp/tcllib-2.0/modules/doctools/doctools.tcl:682-739) uses this object-command spelling (`$mpip eval [list ...]`, `$mpip invokehidden source ...`, `$mpip eval fmt_numpasses`) far more than the literal `interp eval $mpip {...}` form the idx=9 repro tests. A fix that only touches handle_interp_alias and handle_interp_eval_command (the two sites the root-cause hint names) would close the minimal repro but leave the actual motivating file's dominant idiom still broken. Must also fix handle_interp_handle_eval_command's `cmd_name` resolution (included above as its own proposed change).

2. (Pre-existing, independent of idx=9, but the natural fix for idx=9 either fixes or perpetuates it depending on implementation) `handle_interp_eval_command`'s existing dynamic-path branch keys the synthetic child scope by the dynamic word's raw source *text* (e.g. literally the string "$s"), not by call-site identity. Empirically confirmed live (scratchpad/audit/e2): two unrelated procs each doing `set s [interp create -safe]; interp eval $s { proc helper {...}; helper }` with different bodies collapse into ONE shared `@interp@$s`-ish domain — `references` on one proc's `helper` definition returns 3 locations spanning both procs, and go-to-definition from one proc's call resolves into the other proc's definition. This is the exact class of bug commit 26e5553 (same session, same #923 branch) fixed for `namespace eval $name {...}` / `oo::define $class ...` (via per-call-site `@dynns@<offset>` / `@dynclass@<offset>` keys) — but a comment 26e5553 itself added (handlers.rs ~1044-1046, in handle_namespace_eval_command) claims interp eval's dynamic-path handling "mirrors" that fix and "is conservatively isolated the same way rather than merged by raw text." That claim does not hold for the current code; it was either aspirational or an oversight. The proposed fix above (resolve_dynamic_interp_path returning the new per-call-site `@autoname@<offset>` key instead of raw text, consumed by handle_interp_eval_command) closes this for the TRACKED subset (handles that trace back to a `set VAR [interp create ...]`) as a side effect of fixing idx=9, but a residual gap remains for untracked dynamic paths (e.g. a proc parameter used directly as an interp eval path) — flag this clearly to the implementer so they don't claim full parity with 26e5553's fix when only the tracked subset is actually covered; a full fix of the untracked case would need the same offset-based-fallback treatment 26e5553 gave namespace/class targets, applied to handle_interp_eval_command's final else-branch too, as a separate follow-up.

3. (Confirms the fix's design constraint, not a bug in itself) Nested `interp create` — even with a fully literal path — never reaches handle_interp_create_command at all today when it's wrapped in a `[...]` command substitution, because commands.rs's nested-substitution dispatcher (dispatch_nested_segment / run_nested_command_diagnostics, commands.rs:1656-1786, doc comment at 1718-1719) intentionally dispatches only a curated subset of handler families (diagnostics, var-binding commands, proc/oo::define, and — explicitly — only the two `package` hooks) and does NOT route Hook::InterpCreate/InterpAlias/InterpEval. Verified live (scratchpad/audit/d): `set s [interp create -safe literalName]` followed by top-level `interp alias literalName ...` / `interp eval literalName {...}` produces a spurious `W140 interpreter 'literalName' is never created in this file`, and go-to-definition on the aliased command still fails, despite the path being fully literal. This means the correct fix cannot rely on "make interp create reachable via the general nested-dispatch machinery" (that would be a much bigger, riskier change touching every nested-substitution command) — it must instead detect the `set VAR [interp create ...]` shape directly and locally, exactly the way record_instance_creation/class_from_constructor_subst already do for TclOO constructors, which is what the proposed fix does. Implementer should be aware this nested-dispatch gap is real and general (it is not special to interp create) but is being worked around, not fixed, by this plan — scoped exactly to the shape the finding is about.

Also note: `instance_classes` (types.rs:847, the closest existing "set VAR [CONSTRUCTOR ...]" precedent to imitate) is intentionally flat/non-scoped/last-write-wins across the whole file, and is explicitly documented as such (with a companion `HashSet` — types.rs:856-869 — that exists specifically so ONE consumer that needs soundness can detect and abstain on a collision, rather than trust last-write-wins). This is an accepted trade-off for that consumer (a wrong class label only softens a method-validation diagnostic), but reproduction (2) above proves the identical flat-keying approach is unsafe for interpreter domains (it corrupts go-to-definition results, not just a diagnostic). Flagging this explicitly so the implementer doesn't default to copying instance_classes's flat HashMap<String,String> shape out of familiarity — the scope-chain-aware const_strings shape must be used instead.

Exact synthetic-key naming convention for the no-literal-path case (`@autoname@<offset>` was used throughout this plan as a placeholder, parallel to 26e5553's `@dynns@`/`@dynclass@`) — pick whatever reads best alongside `@interp@`; whatever is chosen should be pinned by a unit test the way handle_namespace_eval_dynamic_target_gets_a_synthetic_span_keyed_name (handlers.rs:4583) pins `@dynns@15`, since downstream consumers (symbols/go-to-def) will surface this string.

2. Whether to prefix the synthetic no-literal-path key with the enclosing `interp_path_stack` (for a `set VAR [interp create -safe]` written inside a nested `interp eval` body, i.e. a dynamically-named grandchild interpreter) — not required for correctness (raw source offset is already globally unique) but would be more consistent with how literal paths are qualified via `qualified_interp_key`. Low-stakes stylistic choice; either is sound.

3. Whether to also extend `handle_interp_delete_command` / `apply_interp_visibility_delta` (proposed change #9, optional) in the same PR or as a fast-follow — doctools.tcl does call `interp delete $mpip`, but leaving it as today's conservative `dynamic_interp_ops = true` is safe (no false negatives beyond today's baseline), just imprecise (suppresses W140 file-wide rather than just for that interpreter). approach_summary:
Two independent, separately-landable fixes, verified against live tclsh9.0.4/8.6.14 and a freshly-built tcl-lsp-server binary (built after the current HEAD, commit 26e5553 — confirmed via git log that none of this session's 4 recent fixes touch these files).

PART A — W123 false positive on bare exists/get inside ::tcl::dict (HIGH confidence). Root cause: dict.rs registers "exists"/"get"/etc. only as SubCommand entries of the "dict" ensemble spec, never as standalone qualified CommandSpecs, so the registry has no entry for "::tcl::dict::exists" even though tclsh confirms it's a real, separately-invocable command. Separately, unresolved.rs's w123_invocation_resolves only checks a flat/bare registry_names set plus flat tail-name sets — it never walks the call's enclosing namespace the way real Tcl bare-name resolution does. Critically, that namespace-walk machinery ALREADY EXISTS and is ALREADY CORRECT: SignatureCommandInvocation.resolution_candidates (signature_scan/types.rs) is populated for every invocation by Analyser::finalise_invocation_resolutions (analyser/scope.rs), which calls tcl_syntax::naming::command_resolution_candidates using the call's namespace from Analyser::command_resolution_namespace — and I verified by reading advance_command_resolution_namespace's ScopeKind::Proc arm that it already derives "::tcl::dict" as the resolution namespace for a bare call inside `proc ::tcl::dict::getnull {...}` (from the proc's own qualified name, not lexical `namespace eval` nesting — matching real Tcl). So resolution_candidates for the bare `exists` call is ALREADY `["::tcl::dict::exists", "::exists"]` today; the only missing piece is a registry entry for the first candidate. Fix = (1) add qualified specs to the registry, (2) make w123_invocation_resolves consult resolution_candidates against the same registry_names set it already checks for the bare name.

PART B — W001 false positive on `dict getnull` at the call site, plus its inconsistency with hover/definition (MEDIUM confidence). Root cause: dict's SUBCOMMANDS array is static; it can't reflect tcllib dicttool.tcl's runtime `namespace ensemble configure dict -map [dict replace [namespace ensemble configure dict -map] getnull ::tcl::dict::getnull]` patch (verified this is the REAL tcllib idiom, repeated identically 5 times in the real tcllib-2.0 dicttool.tcl for getnull/print/is_dict/rmerge/isnull). I traced hover/definition's apparent "correct" resolution precisely: it is NOT ensemble-aware — tcl-lsp-core's definition()/hover() treat ANY bareword under the cursor as a potential call and resolve it via resolve_called_proc → fallback_proc_by_simple_name, a document-wide, position-blind, namespace-blind simple-name scan that happens to find `proc ::tcl::dict::getnull` only because it's the sole proc in the file named "getnull" — not because anything verified the ensemble map was actually patched. So "unifying" W001 with hover/definition doesn't require touching hover/definition (it's already lenient); it requires giving W001 the SAME underlying fact (a proc exists at the conventional namespace-qualified name) but checked more precisely (namespace-scoped, via a new CommandSpec.implementation_namespace field) than hover's blind scan.

proposed_changes.description: Add a function that derives one standalone CommandSpec per existing SUBCOMMANDS entry, named "::tcl::dict::<name>" (e.g. "::tcl::dict::exists", "::tcl::dict::get"), EXCLUDING "getd" — verified live against tclsh9.0.4 and tclsh8.6.14 that `info commands ::tcl::dict::*` never lists ::tcl::dict::getd under either version (it is purely an ensemble-map unambiguous-prefix alias of getdef, resolved by Tcl's ensemble dispatch itself, never a registered command); every OTHER SUBCOMMANDS entry (append, create, exists, filter, for, get, incr, keys, lappend, map, merge, remove, replace, set, size, unset, update, values, with, info, getdef, getwithdefault — 22 names) DOES have a real backing command, confirmed live. Each synthesized spec must set `dialects: sub.dialects.or(spec().dialects)` (i.e. fall back to dict's own TCL85_PLUS gate, read from the single source of truth, never hardcoded a second time, and never left `None` — `None` means "available under every dialect" per CommandSpec's own doc, which would wrongly make these appear available even under f5-irules/EDA dialects that have no dict at all). Carry over arity/detail/synopsis/return_type verbatim from the SubCommand (verified via tclsh that `::tcl::dict::exists $d a` and `dict exists $d a` take identical arguments — only the wrong-#args error message's command-name prefix differs). Register ONLY the qualified spelling, never a bare "exists"/"get" CommandSpec — bare exists/get outside ::tcl::dict must stay genuinely unknown (tclsh-confirmed: `exists foo bar` at global/other-namespace scope errors "invalid command name"). Add a small unit test asserting the output never contains a spec named "::tcl::dict::getd" and that its length equals SUBCOMMANDS.len() - 1, to guard against silent drift if SUBCOMMANDS ever gains/loses an entry.
proposed_changes.existing_pattern_to_reuse: Mirrors the already-established "multiple spellings of one command" convention: tcl_zipfs.rs's make_spec(name) helper called once for "zipfs" and once for "::tcl::zipfs" (spec()/spec_qualified()), and tcl_process.rs's identical pattern — just applied per-subcommand instead of per-whole-spec, closer in shape to mathop_generated.rs (one CommandSpec per ensemble member, multiple qualified spellings).

proposed_changes.description: Add `specs.extend(dict::qualified_specs());` immediately next to the existing `specs.extend(mathop_generated::specs());` (line 190) — identical idiom, same function, same aggregation point.
proposed_changes.existing_pattern_to_reuse: specs.extend(mathop_generated::specs()) — the exact same aggregation call shape, one line above.

proposed_changes.function_or_area: w123_invocation_resolves (~line 341) and its caller emit_w123_for_invocations (~line 418, the call at ~line 448)
proposed_changes.description: Add a 4th parameter `resolution_candidates: &[String]` to w123_invocation_resolves. Insert a new check immediately after the existing `if name.contains("::") || name.starts_with('$') || name.starts_with('[') { return true; }` block and before the `known.proc_tail_names.contains(name) || ...` block: `if resolution_candidates.iter().any(|cand| known.registry_names.contains(cand)) { return true; }`. Update the call site to `self.w123_invocation_resolves(known, name, inv.range, &inv.resolution_candidates)`. No changes needed to W123KnownNames or build_w123_known_names — this reuses the exact same registry_names HashSet already built there, just also matching qualified (::-containing) entries in it (which Part A's new specs populate) against the invocation's own precomputed candidate list.
proposed_changes.existing_pattern_to_reuse: SignatureCommandInvocation.resolution_candidates + Analyser::finalise_invocation_resolutions (analyser/scope.rs) + tcl_syntax::naming::command_resolution_candidates — all already correctly compute and store the exact Tcl-priority-ordered qualified candidate list per invocation, including for this exact dict.rs scenario; confirmed by reading resolve_command_qualified_name and advance_command_resolution_namespace's ScopeKind::Proc arm, which already derives a proc's DEFINING namespace (::tcl::dict for `proc ::tcl::dict::getnull`) rather than lexical namespace-eval nesting. This is the 'bare name relative to enclosing lexical namespace' path the root-cause hint says is missing — it was already built for the arity-shadow/rename-safety features and just never consulted by W123.

proposed_changes.description: Add `pub implementation_namespace: Option<&'static str>` to CommandSpec, default None. Set `Some("::tcl::dict")` in dict.rs's spec(). This is also the correct place for Part A's qualified_specs() to read its namespace prefix from (avoid a second hardcoded "::tcl::dict" literal).

proposed_changes.function_or_area: emit_w001_unknown_subcommand (~line 669), specifically right after the existing `if self.check_disabled_in_other_dialect_subcommand(...) { return; }` block (~line 749-753) and before `let ns = self.command_resolution_namespace(scope_path);`
proposed_changes.description: PRIMARY (recommended) fix — add: `if self.dynamic_ensemble_subcommand_known(cmd_name, first_arg) { return; }` with a new private method: `fn dynamic_ensemble_subcommand_known(&self, cmd_name: &str, first_arg: &str) -> bool { let Some(registry) = self.registry else { return false }; let Some(spec) = registry.get(cmd_name) else { return false }; let Some(ns) = spec.implementation_namespace else { return false }; self.result.all_procs.contains_key(&format!("{ns}::{first_arg}")) }`. Needs no new analyser-state field and no per-item/snapshot plumbing since all_procs is already globally merged before diagnostics run (run_diagnostic_emitters order). This deliberately does NOT verify that `namespace ensemble configure dict -map` was actually called in the file — see open_questions for the precision tradeoff and the optional hardening.
proposed_changes.existing_pattern_to_reuse: self.registry (already used at the top of this same function: `if self.registry.is_none() { return; }`) and self.result.all_procs (already the backbone of proc-tail resolution elsewhere, e.g. unresolved.rs's proc_tail_names).

proposed_changes.description: OPTIONAL precision hardening (not required for the primary fix above): widen the `if args[1] != "create" { return; }` gate to also accept "configure", and record a bare (::-stripped) fact into a new `reconfigured_ensembles: HashSet<String>` whenever `namespace ensemble configure <name> -map ...` is seen (regardless of whether the -map value can be parsed — presence alone is the signal). IMPORTANT structural difference from `create`: for `configure`, args[2] is the MANDATORY explicit ensemble name (create's name is often implicit/ambient), so options start at args[3..], not args[2..] — the existing opts/opt_tokens slicing must branch on which subcommand matched. If implemented, dynamic_ensemble_subcommand_known above should additionally check `self.reconfigured_ensembles.contains(cmd_name.trim_start_matches(':'))`.
proposed_changes.existing_pattern_to_reuse: record_ensemble_map_targets already exists in this same function for the `create` form's `-map` option (though its list_word_elements whitespace-split only handles a literal {...} list, not tcllib's `[dict replace [...] ...]` command-substitution shape — reusing it as-is is not sufficient, only its presence as prior art for 'this file touches this ensemble's map' is relevant here). The new HashSet<String> field should mechanically replicate ensemble_namespaces's existing plumbing exactly: declare+init in analyser/state.rs (~line 343), populate in this handler, thread through per_item.rs's BodyFragment (struct field ~line 553, capture ~line 680, merge-at-graft ~line 442) for full correctness, and deliberately SKIP snapshot.rs — confirmed ensemble_namespaces is documented there (line 145) as intentionally excluded from snapshot/restore ('will be rebuilt as the walk continues'), and the same reasoning applies unchanged to this new field.

test_scenarios.description: Primary repro (tcllib dicttool.tcl idiom), TWO diagnostics that must disappear after the fix: (1) W123 on bare `exists`/`get` — `if {[::info commands ::tcl::dict::getnull] eq {}} { proc ::tcl::dict::getnull {dictionary args} { if {[exists $dictionary {*}$args]} { get $dictionary {*}$args } } ; namespace ensemble configure dict -map [dict replace [namespace ensemble configure dict -map] getnull ::tcl::dict::getnull] }` — currently fires 'W123 Unknown command exists; did you mean exit?' and 'W123 Unknown command get; did you mean gets?'; must fire neither after Part A. (2) W001 on the call site — `proc demo {} { set clay [dict create a 1 b 2]; return [dict getnull $clay a] }` in the same file — currently fires 'W001 Unknown subcommand getnull for dict'; must not fire after Part B. Live-confirmed today via the lsp-client skill's `diagnostics` subcommand against a freshly-built server.

Isolation of the W123 half with NO ensemble-configure call anywhere in the file (proves Part A is not accidentally coupled to Part B / the ensemble-configure detection): `proc ::tcl::dict::myhelper {d k} { if {[exists $d $k]} { return [get $d $k] } ; return MISSING }` called as `::tcl::dict::myhelper [dict create a 1 b 2] a`. Currently fires 2x W123 (verified live); must fire 0 after Part A alone.

A second sibling block from the same real tcllib idiom, to prove the fix isn't overfit to 'getnull': `proc ::tcl::dict::is_dict {d} { if {[catch {dict size $d} err]} { return 0 } ; return 1 } ; namespace ensemble configure dict -map [dict replace [namespace ensemble configure dict -map] is_dict ::tcl::dict::is_dict]` then a call site `dict is_dict $x`. Must produce 0 W123/W001 after both parts of the fix (note this block doesn't call bare exists/get, so it exercises Part B only).

Control (must KEEP firing — tclsh-confirmed real error): bare `exists`/`get` called OUTSIDE ::tcl::dict, e.g. at global scope or inside an unrelated proc — `proc foo {} { return [exists bar] }` or top-level `exists foo bar`. tclsh: 'invalid command name "exists"'. Must still fire W123 after Part A — this is the critical regression guard proving the fix is properly namespace-scoped, not a blanket allow-list for 'exists'/'get'.

Control (must KEEP firing): `proc demo3 {} { set d [dict create a 1 b 2] ; return [dict zzzznotreal $d a] }` — a genuinely nonexistent dict subcommand, no proc named zzzznotreal exists anywhere. Must still fire W001 after Part B (already live-confirmed as firing today; regression-guard that the new dynamic_ensemble_subcommand_known check doesn't over-suppress).

Ordinary user-namespace bare-name resolution, unrelated to dict: `namespace eval ::foo { proc helper {} { return 42 } ; proc bar {} { return [helper] } } ; puts [::foo::bar]`. Already 0 diagnostics (live-confirmed); must remain 0 — regression guard that Part A's new resolution_candidates check doesn't change behavior for the common case (it's a no-op there since the bare-name check already resolves it earlier in w123_invocation_resolves).

Fully-qualified calls to the real builtins, no ensemble patch: `proc demo2 {} { set d [dict create a 1 b 2] ; if {[::tcl::dict::exists $d a]} { return [::tcl::dict::get $d a] } }`. Already 0 diagnostics (live-confirmed); must remain 0 — proves the qualified-name path (which already worked via the `name.contains("::")` conservative-skip in w123_invocation_resolves) is untouched by the fix.

Existing W001 regression suite must be unaffected by Part B: `string bogus hello` (still fires W001), `string le abc` (unique-prefix abbreviation, still 0 diagnostics), `zipfs bogus x` under tcl9.0 (still fires W001), `proc string {op args} {...}\nstring reverse x` (proc-shadow suppression, still 0 W001) — these are existing tests in rust/tcl-compiler/tests/analyser.rs (~lines 387-484); run them unchanged as a regression pass, since dynamic_ensemble_subcommand_known only activates for commands whose spec sets implementation_namespace (only dict, after this fix), so string/zipfs/etc. take the Some(spec) branch but hit `implementation_namespace == None` and return false immediately.

Explicit, ACKNOWLEDGED precision gap in the PRIMARY (simple) Part-B design — flagged here so the implementer can consciously accept it or build the optional hardening instead: `proc ::tcl::dict::stray {d} { return $d }` defined but the ensemble's -map is NEVER reconfigured to include it, then called as `dict stray $x`. Real tclsh: 'unknown or ambiguous subcommand "stray": must be ...' (genuine error) — W001 SHOULD fire. Under the primary fix (implementation_namespace + all_procs lookup only, no configure-observed gate), this will be WRONGLY suppressed (a new false negative), because the check only requires a same-named proc to exist at the conventional location, not proof the -map was patched. This is exactly what the optional 'reconfigured_ensembles' hardening (see proposed_changes) closes; recommend the implementer decide explicitly rather than discover this by accident.

Code-actions / harmful-quickfix regression guard, end-to-end: at the `exists` call site inside `::tcl::dict::getnull` (or the isolated myhelper repro), request code actions over the diagnostic's own range. Today this returns `[quickfix] Replace with 'exit'` with edit `Replace <span> with: 'exit'` (live-confirmed) — applying it turns `if {[exists $dictionary {*}$args]} {...}` into `if {[exit $dictionary {*}$args]} {...}`, which terminates the process. After the fix (W123 no longer fires there), this quickfix must not be offered at all. Mirror the existing 'no replacement action' idiom in rust/tcl-lsp-server/tests/e2e/code_actions.rs (test_w123_no_replacement_without_near_candidate / test_w001_no_action_for_unique_prefix_abbreviation).

Dialect-gating regression guard for Part A's new qualified specs (guards secondary issue #4): under a dialect/profile with no `dict` at all (or an 8.4-only profile, below dict's own TCL85_PLUS gate), a bare `exists`/`get` inside a proc lexically written under `::tcl::dict` must still fire W123 (or, if `dict` itself is simply absent from that profile, whatever the existing behavior is for `dict`) — i.e. the new `::tcl::dict::exists` spec's `dialects` field must correctly inherit dict's own gate rather than defaulting to `None` (=all dialects), which would wrongly make it 'known' under e.g. f5-irules where dict was never loaded this way.

open_questions:
1. Part B design decision (needs a human/implementer call, not something I should decide unilaterally): should emit_w001_unknown_subcommand's new check require observing an actual `namespace ensemble configure <cmd> -map` call in the file (the more precise, higher-implementation-cost 'optional hardening' variant, which needs new HashSet<String> state threaded through state.rs/handlers.rs/per_item.rs), or is 'a proc exists at <implementation_namespace>::<subcommand>' alone an acceptable signal (the simpler primary variant, which has the acknowledged FN gap in test_scenarios)? I lean toward shipping the simple variant first (it's a strict, easily-reasoned-about, low-blast-radius suppression, and the FN it introduces is narrow and arguably matches this project's existing risk tolerance — e.g. W123's blanket 'any package require suppresses W123 file-wide' is a far larger conservative-suppression precedent already in the codebase) but this is a judgment call the task asked me not to make silently.
2. Should Part A's qualified_specs() mechanism be generalized (e.g. driven generically off CommandSpec.implementation_namespace at registry-build time in registry.rs, expanding ANY future ensemble that sets the field, rather than a dict.rs-local hand-written name list) versus the more contained, dict-only, zero-new-infrastructure version I proposed? I chose the contained version because dict is currently the ONLY ensemble in this registry that needs this treatment (string/array/info are C switch-statements with no backing implementation namespace of individually-callable commands) — a generic auto-expansion mechanism would need either build-time codegen (like mathop_generated.rs, generated by a checked-in script) or a runtime Box::leak per synthesized name (which DOES have one precedent in this codebase, cache.rs:58, but only for leaking the whole registry, not per-string) to keep CommandSpec.name as &'static str. I'd defer this generalization until a second ensemble actually needs it, per the codebase's own 'migration debt is tracked, not grandfathered, not preemptively built' philosophy — but flagging so the implementer can disagree.
3. I did not verify whether `clock` (implemented substantially via Tcl-level procs under ::tcl::clock::*) has the same 'bare name resolves from inside its own implementation namespace' property and thus the same latent W123 gap — it almost certainly does by the same C-Tcl-ensemble-implementation-namespace mechanism, but it's a separate finding/file (tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/clock_.rs) outside idx=105's confirmed scope; worth a follow-up differential-audit pass if the team wants full coverage of this class of bug rather than just the dict instance.
secondary_issues_found:
(1) registry_name_deleted_before (unresolved.rs) only tracks deletion of a BARE global builtin via a `\"::{name}\"` key convention; a hypothetical `rename ::tcl::dict::exists {}` wouldn't be caught by Part A's new candidate check (the renamed-away name would still resolve). Extremely rare shape, pre-existing limitation shared by the rest of the file's design, not a regression from this fix — flagging only for completeness.
(2) Completion for `dict <TAB>` will still not suggest \"getnull\" after the Part B fix (SUBCOMMANDS is unchanged, only the diagnostic-suppression path is touched) — a coverage/UX gap, not a regression, plausibly acceptable/out of scope for this finding but worth a one-line note to the implementer so it isn't mistaken for an incomplete fix.
(3) hover/definition's fallback_proc_by_simple_name (tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs) is a genuinely over-broad, POSITION-BLIND, document-wide simple-name match — not specific to ensembles or dict at all. It resolves ANY bareword under the cursor (whether it's a command head or merely an argument/subcommand word of some other command) to any proc anywhere in the file sharing that simple name, when no namespace-visible candidate exists. It happens to produce the 'right' answer for `dict getnull` purely because that's the only proc named \"getnull\" in the file. This means: (a) it would equally 'resolve' `dict someOtherWord` to an unrelated same-named proc elsewhere in the file even with no ensemble patch at all, and (b) a future, unrelated tightening of this fallback (someone making it more conservative for a different bug) could silently reintroduce a hover/W001 divergence from the opposite direction, since W001 (after this fix) and hover currently reach the same conclusion via genuinely different, uncoordinated mechanisms. I'm not proposing to fix this now (it's pre-existing and not what idx=105's FAILURE SCENARIO is centered on), but recommend the implementer at least leave a code comment cross-referencing dynamic_ensemble_subcommand_known so a future reader knows the two are only coincidentally aligned, not structurally unified.
(4) Verified live that dict's own CommandSpec dialect gate is DialectSet::TCL85_PLUS (registry.rs commands/tcl/dict.rs spec()) — Part A's qualified_specs() MUST inherit this (via the new implementation_namespace-adjacent `spec().dialects` read, or equivalent) rather than defaulting new specs to `dialects: None`, which the CommandSpec doc explicitly defines as 'available in all dialects' — an easy, silent mistake that would make e.g. `::tcl::dict::exists` wrongly 'available' under f5-irules/EDA profiles that never load dict at all. Called out explicitly in proposed_changes and given its own regression test scenario.
(5) Verified live (tclsh8.6.14 AND tclsh9.0.4) that \"getd\" is excluded from `info commands ::tcl::dict::*` under BOTH versions — it is an ensemble-map-only unambiguous-prefix alias of \"getdef\", never itself a registered command. A naive implementation that loops over ALL of SUBCOMMANDS without this exclusion would introduce a new, subtly-wrong CommandSpec for a command that doesn't exist (::tcl::dict::getd) — precisely the class of un-verified-against-tclsh mistake this project's process is designed to catch. Flagged with its own regression test.

Root cause confirmed exactly as hinted: record_ensemble_map_targets (handlers.rs ~1694) and record_ensemble_subcommands (~1708) each call push_command_reference for the -map/-subcommands TARGET only — no subcommand->target table is ever persisted anywhere queryable by the LSP. definition()/hover()/references() never look at "is the preceding word a known ensemble" at all.

Existing-pattern search (AGENTS.md's registry/reuse mandate): command_aliases (interp alias table) is the closest architectural analog but cannot be reused directly — it's a flat `name -> target` map keyed by a name that's independently callable; an ensemble subcommand ("make") is never independently callable (only `widget make` as a pair dispatches), and two different ensembles can share a subcommand name, so a *nested* `ensemble_qualified_name -> {subcommand -> target}` table is required — new state, not reuse of command_aliases itself. bareword_resolution_candidates (tcl_syntax::naming, already used by resolve_class_target_at) is the right reuse for namespace-qualifying the ensemble head. instance_method_at_cursor (definition.rs) is the right reuse for finding "the single token immediately preceding this word, bounded by `;`/`[`/`{`/line-start" — I discovered empirically that the registry's OWN existing ensemble-subcommand hover (subcommand_hover_text, used for string/dict/info) does NOT handle this shape (it naively splits the whole LINE, so `puts [string length foo]` — the exact nesting our own repro uses — returns "(no hover)" even for a builtin; verified live). instance_method_at_cursor already correctly handles `[...]`-nested calls, so it — not the registry pattern — is the correct template. process_command's existing `call PROC` iRules-indirection block (commands.rs 374-396, "push an extra command_invocations entry for an indirect target") is a near-exact precedent for how to make find-references/rename/call-hierarchy pick up ensemble call sites for free, including its existence_probe:true convention (issue #945 fault 9) for a name that's referenceable but never independently resolvable.

Deep-dived the cross-file (main.tcl -> widget.tcl) repro specifically since the finding presents it as confirmed evidence too. Empirically PROVEN (with a properly-scoped 2-file workspace root and a 4s settle delay to rule out a scan race) that this is a SEPARATE, deeper gap: W123 fires "Unknown command 'widget'" on every main.tcl call site even though widget.tcl (in the same workspace) declares the ensemble — meaning cross-file ensemble awareness doesn't exist at all today, for either W123 suppression or navigation. proposed_changes.description: Add `pub ensemble_subcommand_targets: HashMap<String, HashMap<String, String>>`. Outer key = the ensemble's own resolved/qualified invocable command name (e.g. "::widget", "::e") — same identity as what handle_namespace_ensemble already inserts into ensemble_namespaces. Inner key = subcommand exactly as written in the -map/-subcommands list (e.g. "make"). Inner value = the target's resolved qualified command name (e.g. "::widget::Make"). Must live on AnalysisResult (not on Analyser, unlike ensemble_namespaces) because tcl-lsp-core's providers only ever see &AnalysisResult — confirmed by reading definition.rs/hover.rs/references.rs signatures. AnalysisResult already derives Debug/Clone/Default/PartialEq, all satisfied automatically by the nested HashMap. VERIFIED no snapshot.rs change is needed: AnalyserSnapshot.result is a wholesale AnalysisResult::clone()/restore (read snapshot.rs in full), not a field-by-field enumeration, so the new field is captured/restored for free.

This must be resolved BEFORE processing -map/-subcommands regardless of option order (Tcl doesn't require -command before -map; none of the confirmed repros exercise reordering, but a proper pre-scan is ~5 lines and avoids a silent wrong-key bug for -map-before-command). Thread `&ensemble_key` into record_ensemble_map_targets and record_ensemble_subcommands as a new parameter (in addition to scope_path, which is still needed to resolve each TARGET's own qualified name).

3) While tracing the right consumer-side pattern to reuse, discovered that the EXISTING registry-driven ensemble-subcommand hover (subcommand_hover_text in hover.rs, used for string/dict/info/etc.) is itself broken for a command nested inside `[...]` — verified live: `string length foo` at top level hovers correctly (\"Subcommand of `string`\"), but the exact same cursor position inside `puts [string length foo]` returns \"(no hover)\", because the helper naively splits the whole source LINE on whitespace rather than finding the enclosing command segment. This is a pre-existing, independent bug (not part of idx=106, and not something this fix touches or regresses), but it directly shaped the design: it ruled out copying that pattern for the new ensemble logic (which would have silently failed on the repro's own `puts [e foo bar]` / `puts [widget make hello]` shapes) in favor of instance_method_at_cursor's segment-bounded scan, which IS bracket-aware and was verified correct for this exact nesting. Worth its own separate finding/ticket given it affects existing, shipped, registry-builtin hover (string/dict/info/etc. subcommands), likely higher severity than idx=106 itself since it's a regression-risk-free, high-value, self-contained fix (swap subcommand_hover_text's line-splitting for instance_method_at_cursor's segment-scan, or a proper token-based approach).

4) Pre-existing, minor, unrelated-but-adjacent inaccuracy noticed while reading handle_namespace_ensemble: ensemble_namespaces unconditionally inserts the enclosing namespace `ns` even when `-command NAME` is also given, but verified against tclsh9.0 that in that case the bare namespace name is NOT actually a valid command (`info commands ::foo` is empty; calling it errors \"invalid command name\") — only the -command value is real. This is pinned by existing tests (handle_namespace_ensemble_command_option_recorded asserts BOTH names present) so it's an accepted, intentional leniency, not something to silently change. My new ensemble_key computation for the NEW table does NOT inherit this leniency (it picks exactly one correct key), so the new table won't propagate the same minor inaccuracy — but flagging it in case the implementer wants to tighten ensemble_namespaces itself in a follow-up (would need a test update, out of scope here).

5) The -map value's target CAN, per Tcl's ensemble semantics, itself be a multi-word list (prepended extra arguments, akin to interp alias), not just a bare command name. list_word_elements's naive whitespace-splitting (used by both the existing reverse-direction code and my new forward-direction code) does not handle this — a pre-existing limitation inherited unchanged by this fix, not something it makes worse. None of the confirmed repro's examples use this shape, so out of scope here; noted for completeness."

None of this session's other landed fixes (idx 107/115, 111, 118/119) touch this path.

Root cause, traced precisely through the current code: `namespace eval`/`namespace inscope` both dispatch to `handle_namespace_eval_command` (both subcommands stamp `analyser_hook: Some(AnalyserHookId::NamespaceEval)` — rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/namespace_.rs:220 and :275). For `namespace eval $ns [list namespace unknown $handler]`, that function computes `body_tok = arg_tokens.get(2)` — a `TokenType::Cmd` token (a `[...]` command substitution is always Cmd per AGENTS.md's lexer-token-type table, never Str) — and calls `self.analyse_body(&text, tok, &child_path)`. `analyse_body` (rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/commands.rs:114-117) opens with `if body_tok.kind != TokenType::Str { return; }`, so it bails immediately: only a literal braced `{...}` body is ever walked as a script. The `namespace`/`unknown` words hidden inside `[list namespace unknown $handler]` are therefore never visited as a command node by this path. Separately, `process_command`'s generic nested-substitution scan (`record_nested_invocations_from_args` → `record_invocations_from_cmd_token`, and `run_nested_command_diagnostics` → `dispatch_nested_segment`, commands.rs:401/425) DOES descend into `[list namespace unknown $handler]` and correctly identifies it as a call to `list` — but `dispatch_nested_segment` (commands.rs:1656) deliberately runs only syntactic/diagnostic emitters plus an explicit allow-list of exactly `PackageRequire`/`PackageProvide` hooks (commands.rs:1721-1729, "the substitution path deliberately dispatches no other handler family") — never `AnalyserHookId::NamespaceUnknown`, and the resolved `cmd_name` there is `"list"` anyway, not `"namespace"`, so `Hook::NamespaceUnknown` (which lives on the `namespace` command's `unknown` subcommand, commands.rs:736-739 → handlers.rs:3020 `handle_namespace_unknown_command`, which flips `self.result.has_dynamic_providers = true`) can never fire for this shape by any existing path. Confirmed against the real tcllib source: tmp/tcllib-2.0/modules/namespacex/namespacex.tcl:157-162 (`hook::Set`) contains exactly `namespace eval $ns [list namespace unknown $handler]` at line 160, matching the finding verbatim.

Fix: add a small, narrow shape-recogniser, invoked from `handle_namespace_eval_command` right where `body_tok` is computed, that descends a `Cmd`-kind body token one level (reusing the exact CST-descent primitives — `cmd_fragments` + `descend_token` + `segments_from_tree` — already used identically three times in commands.rs for nested-substitution discovery) and, when the resulting segment's words are literally `list namespace unknown ?HANDLER?`, calls the EXISTING `handle_namespace_unknown_command` unmodified with a synthesised `["unknown", HANDLER?]` args slice — reusing its established empty/query-form gating rather than reimplementing it. `has_dynamic_providers` stays a file-wide flag (matching the literal form's own existing, documented file-wide suppression) — no registry changes and no new shared infrastructure are required; this is a pure tcl-compiler analyser-side fix.

proposed_changes.function_or_area: New method Analyser::detect_list_wrapped_namespace_unknown, placed near the other nested-substitution-descent helpers (e.g. directly after record_invocations_from_cmd_token, ~line 1501, or just before cmd_fragments at ~line 1795). No new imports needed — SourceMap, Token, TokenType, descend_token, segments_from_tree, SegmentedCommand are already imported at the top of this file.
proposed_changes.description: pub(super) fn detect_list_wrapped_namespace_unknown(&mut self, body_tok: Token) { if body_tok.kind != TokenType::Cmd { return; } let config = self.lexer_config(); let segs: Vec<SegmentedCommand> = { let sm = SourceMap::new(&self.source); let mut segs = Vec::new(); for frag in self.cmd_fragments(body_tok, config) { if frag.kind != TokenType::Cmd || sm.token_text(frag).is_empty() { continue; } let descended = descend_token(&sm, frag, config); segs.extend(segments_from_tree(descended.tree(), &sm)); } segs }; for seg in &segs { if seg.texts.len() < 3 || seg.texts.len() > 4 { continue; } if seg.texts[0] != "list" || seg.texts[1] != "namespace" || seg.texts[2] != "unknown" { continue; } self.handle_namespace_unknown_command(&seg.texts[2..]); } }  IMPORTANT borrow-checker note: collect `segs` fully inside the `{ let sm = SourceMap::new(...); ... }` block (which borrows self.source immutably) BEFORE calling the `&mut self` method `handle_namespace_unknown_command` in the loop below — this two-phase collect-then-mutate shape is not optional style, it mirrors record_invocations_from_cmd_token's own existing pattern (commands.rs:1464-1493, comment: 'Collect the inner heads first ... resolve + push afterwards so the immutable source borrow has ended') and avoids a borrow conflict between the SourceMap's borrow of self.source and the later &mut self call.
proposed_changes.existing_pattern_to_reuse: cmd_fragments (commands.rs:1795) + descend_token/segments_from_tree exactly as used by record_invocations_from_cmd_token (commands.rs:1464), collect_substitution_heads (commands.rs:2424) and collect_substitution_segments (commands.rs:2606) — same 're-lex the [...] span as its own tiny script, read off its SegmentedCommand(s)' idiom, minus their extra recursion into further-nested substitutions (unnecessary here: only the outermost `list` call matters). handle_namespace_unknown_command (handlers.rs:3020) is called unmodified, not reimplemented.

Nothing else in this function changes — the existing `if let (Some(text), Some(tok)) = (body_text, body_tok) { self.analyse_body(&text, tok, &child_path); }` call at the bottom is left as-is and continues to correctly no-op for a Cmd-kind body_tok (analyse_body's own Str-only gate is untouched). Because both `namespace eval` and `namespace inscope` share this one handler function (registry: namespace_.rs:220 and :275 both stamp AnalyserHookId::NamespaceEval), this single insertion covers both call forms named in the root-cause hint with no extra branching or duplicated logic.

secondary_issues_found:
1) handle_namespace_eval_command only ever reads args.get(2) as 'the body' and silently drops any words at args[3..] — it does not concatenate multi-word namespace-eval bodies the way `eval`/`uplevel` do (Tcl joins all script-position words with a space before evaluating `namespace eval $ns word1 word2 word3`). This is a separate, pre-existing gap, not caused or fixed by this change — flagging so the implementer doesn't conflate it with this bug or feel obligated to fix it here.
2) has_dynamic_providers is (and remains after this fix) a whole-FILE boolean, not scoped per namespace — installing a namespace-scoped `namespace unknown` handler anywhere suppresses W120/W123 for the entire document, not just calls inside that namespace's handler chain (see diagnostics/unresolved.rs:117 and :562). This is pre-existing, documented behaviour for the literal form (handle_namespace_unknown_command's own doc comment says 'file-wide') that this fix deliberately matches rather than improves, per the root-cause hint's own 'or better, scope the suppression per-namespace' aside — a legitimate but materially larger follow-up (would need a per-namespace suppression set threaded through AnalysisResult and the W123 emitter, not a single bool).
3) The fix is intentionally narrow to the literal `list namespace unknown ...` shape (the exact, attested tcllib idiom). It will not catch equivalent constructions built via `concat`, `format`, `linsert`, string concatenation, or a `list`-building helper proc — see the dedicated 'known remaining gap' FP test scenario above. Worth a one-line note in the new function's doc comment so it reads as a deliberate scope boundary, not an oversight.
4) Minor, unlikely-in-practice robustness gap: the literal-text check requires exactly \"list\"/\"namespace\"/\"unknown\" — a `::`-qualified spelling inside the list (`[list ::namespace unknown $handler]`, or `::list ...`) would not match. Since these are plain data words fed to `list` (never resolved as commands), there is no real reason to qualify them and tcllib itself never does, but it's an easy one-line extension (accept both spellings) if a future finding surfaces it.
5) Verified NOT a conflict: the pre-existing `run_nested_command_diagnostics` → `dispatch_nested_segment` pass (commands.rs:1520, :1656) also descends into this same `[list namespace unknown $handler]` substitution (to run `list`'s own arity/security checks), but it dispatches diagnostics keyed on cmd_name == \"list\" and explicitly runs no Hook family except PackageRequire/PackageProvide (commands.rs:1721-1729) — so there is no double-firing, double-suppression, or ordering dependency between that existing pass and the new detect_list_wrapped_namespace_unknown call; they inspect the same tokens independently for unrelated purposes.
6) Checked the four helpers the task specifically asked about (leading_option_word_count, lookup_var_in_namespace, offset_is_inside_any_definition_body, the @dynns@/@dynclass@/@interp@ synthetic-scope-key convention) — none directly solve this bug: the first three address option-word skipping, variable-scope lookup, and body-offset containment respectively (all orthogonal to command-shape recognition inside a `[...]` substitution); the @dynns@ convention lives in the very same handle_namespace_eval_command function but solves a different problem (keeping unrelated dynamic-namespace-target call sites from collapsing into one symbol scope) and needs no changes for this fix.

approach_summary:
CONFIRMED still present in current code (rebuilt tcl-lsp-server from HEAD of claude/tcl-lsp-issue-923-qzkfqz and drove it live via .claude/skills/lsp-client). `lookup_class_member` (definition.rs ~306-348, unchanged from the hint) and `class_member_hover_text` (hover.rs ~2718-2759, unchanged from the hint, doc comment literally says "same dispatch as lookup_class_member") both walk every class whose body_span contains the cursor and match a bareword unconditionally against methods/class_methods/properties (plus constructor/destructor), with no reachability check. Real TclOO methods/classmethods/properties are never namespace-level commands, so a bareword sibling call only succeeds when something exports it into bareword-callable position — the only such mechanism is oo::Helpers::link, a genuine core TclOO builtin since Tcl 8.6 (TclOOLinkObjCmd in tclOOBasic.c, in the helpCmds table alongside next/nextto/self/classvariable, on every method body's namespace path via ::oo::Helpers; confirmed against tmp/tcl8.6.16 and tmp/tcl9.0.4 C source plus the dedicated doc/link.n man page — NOT merely a tcllib idiom, contrary to what the ooutil.tcl-sourced repro might suggest). `link NAME` / `link {NAME TARGET}`, callable only from inside a method/constructor/destructor body, installs a per-object-namespace alias from NAME to `my TARGET` (TARGET defaults to NAME).

Fix: track per-class which bareword names are link-exposed (and to which real member), then gate the three member-lookup arms behind that tracked fact, redirecting through it to the real target.

1. Registry (rust-registry/src/commands/tcl/oo_link.rs, NEW): give `link` a real CommandSpec (name:"link", dialects: DialectSet::TCL86_PLUS, traits: Traits::LANGUAGE_KEYWORD, arity: at_least(1)), mirroring the existing siblings oo_next.rs/oo_my.rs exactly. `link` currently has ZERO registry entries of its own — the only spec named "link" anywhere is the unrelated EDA-Synopsys design-linking command (rust/tcl-registry/src/commands/eda_synopsys/link.rs, dialects: DialectSet::SYNOPSYS) — confirmed live that this causes a spurious W002 "'link' is disabled in the active dialect profile" on 100% legitimate TclOO `link` usage today (see secondary issues). The registry already supports multiple same-named specs disambiguated per dialect (CommandRegistry::by_name: FxHashMap<String, Vec<CommandSpec>> + best_visible's most-specific-wins rule, registry.rs:465-488) — this is precisely that mechanism's intended use, not a special case.

2. Analyser data (rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/types.rs): add `ClassDef.linked_members: HashMap<String, String>` (alias name -> real member name; alias==target for the one-word form), `Default`-initialised empty.

3. Analyser population (rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/oo.rs, `parse_oo_definition_body`): after Phase 1's `for cmd in &cmds` loop finishes (method_bodies is fully populated, class_def is still `&mut` in scope, before Phase 2 starts), scan each collected method/constructor/destructor body's own TOP-LEVEL statements for a `link`-headed call, mirroring the existing `forward`-TARGET recording a few lines above in the same function and reusing the same primitives `handle_interp_alias`'s sibling `detect_interp_alias` already uses (`crate::naming::is_dynamic_word` to skip a `$var`/`[cmd]`-substituted argument, `crate::tcl_expr_eval::split_tcl_list` to parse each argument word as a 1- or 2-element list — `cmd.texts[i]` is already brace-stripped inner text per this crate's segmenter, confirmed by tracing `word_piece`/`collect_method_body`'s own body_text handling, so no extra unwrapping is needed). Deliberately shallow (top-level statements only, no descent into `if`/`catch`/... body arguments) — this exactly matches the codebase's own existing, accepted scope boundary for this class of "scan a method body for one specific call shape" problem (references.rs's `scan_my_method_region`/`scan_obj_method_region`, which the fix does not otherwise touch, likewise only recurse into `[...]` substitutions, never into literal control-flow body arguments).

4. Consumers — gate, don't remove: in `lookup_class_member` (definition.rs) and `class_member_hover_text` (hover.rs), replace the direct `class_def.methods.get(word)` / `class_def.class_methods.get(word)` / `class_def.properties.get(word)` reads with a lookup through `class_def.linked_members.get(word)` first, then look the resolved TARGET up in methods/class_methods/properties (so `link {shortcut realMethod}` correctly redirects a hover/definition on `shortcut` to `realMethod`'s declaration — a case that currently resolves to nothing at all, a related false-negative this closes, verified live). The `word == "constructor"` / `word == "destructor"` arms are deliberately left UNCHANGED/unconditional — see secondary issues.

Diagnostics (W123) already correctly abstains inside class-method bodies (confirmed still 0 diagnostics on both the buggy and property/classmethod variants) — untouched, no diagnostics.rs change needed.
