primary_function: namespace_context_at / innermost_namespace_at (consumer, definition.rs:1069-1093) paired with Analyser::handle_apply_command (producer, rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/handlers.rs:905)
approach_summary:
Confirmed live (not assumed) against current HEAD via the built tcl-lsp-server: `definition divergence.tcl 21 31` still returns `19:9-19:16` (proc ::lexical::cleanup) instead of ::real::cleanup; hover shows the wrong signature; the app_control.tcl blind-bareword control still fires too. Not incidentally fixed by this session's other landed work. tclsh9.0/8.6 both independently re-verified to print "real::cleanup called with done".

Root cause has TWO independent layers - I verified both by direct experimentation, not just code reading, and this splits the fix cleanly into "do this" vs "don't attempt this":

LAYER 1 (general capability gap, HIGH-confidence bounded fix): command_resolution_namespace_at (tcl-compiler/src/analyser/scope.rs:175) and its wrapper namespace_context_at/innermost_namespace_at (definition.rs:1069-1093) compute the command-resolution namespace purely by descending the Scope tree via body_span containment from the root. handle_apply_command DOES already parse a literal `apply {{params} body ns}` and compute the right body_ns, but the Scope subtree it builds (via per_item::reconstruct_proc_scope, per_item.rs:894) is rooted by unconditionally pushing brand-new Namespace-kind wrapper nodes under global (never reusing an existing node, never giving the wrapper a body_span) - so that subtree is structurally unreachable by the span-containment walk, which requires every ancestor on the path to geometrically contain the query offset. I proved this empirically: `apply {{} {cleanup done} ::real}` written as a literal TOP-LEVEL command with ZERO indirection still resolves "cleanup" to the wrong, lexically-nearest proc today. This is a more fundamental version of the bug than the finding's own phrasing suggests - the finding's "control" case only looked right by coincidence of fallback_proc_by_simple_name's tie-break, and that fallback mechanism (not any part of the apply-aware machinery) is 100% of what decides today's answer in every case I tested.

LAYER 2 (specific to the exact confirmed repro, NOT a bounded/generic fix): divergence.tcl never writes `apply` as a literal/direct command word at all. It's reached two more hops removed: (a) `coroutine co ::apply $lambda` passes `::apply` as coroutine's registry-modeled `command_prefixes` argument (tcl-registry/src/commands/tcl/coroutine.rs:47) - a mechanism the analyser today consults ONLY for IR-level interprocedural call-graph reachability (tcl-compiler/src/interprocedural.rs:1098, feeds the optimizer's dead-code pass), never to re-dispatch through AnalyserHookId::Apply - so handle_apply_command never fires for this call, full stop. I confirmed this is a KNOWN, ALREADY-DOCUMENTED limitation, not my own speculation: rust/tcl-lsp-server/tests/preview_tickets_e2e.rs:750-753 has an existing comment stating "apply is only specially recognised as the head of its own command, not nested inside another command substitution." (b) Even granting (a), the actual "cleanup" token is a plain argument word to `genlib::finally cleanup done` - an ordinary, statically-visible proc call. It becomes a command name only because finally's OWN body (verbatim tcllib generator.tcl:102-105) captures `[uplevel 1 {namespace current}]` and re-injects its own variadic `args` as the body of a NEW, dynamically-built `::apply {args $args $ns}` lambda registered as a coroutine delete-trace. There is no static/lexical connection between "cleanup" and any apply call in the source text - the connection exists only by interpreting finally's runtime behavior. Recognizing this generically (without naming tcllib's generator package, which AGENTS.md's registry-driven/no-per-command-branching convention prohibits) needs a new interprocedural capability ("this proc forwards its args as a script invoked later via a captured dynamic namespace") that doesn't exist anywhere in the codebase - disproportionate scope for a low-severity finding.

RECOMMENDATION: implement the bounded Layer-1 fix (add a flat, span-keyed namespace-override list that hover/definition consult ahead of the lexical scope-chain walk, populated by handle_apply_command, extended to follow one hop of $var/list-substitution indirection). This demonstrably fixes real, verified-broken cases, including simpler ones than the finding's own repro. Do NOT chase Layer 2 in this pass - document divergence.tcl's exact shape as a known, considered limitation.

secondary_issues_found:
1. per_item.rs incremental-path wiring (rebase_fragment + graft_proc_body) is not optional polish - it's required for correctness under on-keystroke/incremental analysis, and is exactly the kind of second root cause that made two other findings this session look 'fixed' while still failing. Any implementation that adds namespace_overrides to AnalysisResult without also touching these two functions will pass a fresh-open-file test and then silently regress the moment the same apply call is edited incrementally inside a proc body.

2. handle_apply_command's existing reconstruct_proc_scope-based subtree construction (per_item.rs:894) is, as far as I can determine and partially confirmed by an existing passing unit test (tcl-compiler/src/analyser/state.rs:1810 apply_body_proc_honours_explicit_lambda_namespace), ENTIRELY INERT for hover/go-to-definition purposes - it can never be reached by the span-containment walk this bug is about, because reconstruct_proc_scope always creates fresh, body_span-less wrapper Namespace nodes disconnected from wherever the body text lexically lives. Its real, working purpose is narrower and separate: registering a nested `proc` DEFINITION written inside the apply body under the correct qualified name in the flat all_procs map (a name-keyed lookup, structurally independent of span-containment). Do not touch or try to 'fix' this mechanism as part of this change - it already works for its own purpose, and the new namespace_overrides list is a deliberately separate, additive mechanism for the namespace-CONTEXT-lookup problem this finding is about.

3. const_strings / resolve_const_word (handlers.rs:154-188, 424-444) never records a command-substitution ([list ...], or any [...]) RHS as a constant at all - handle_set_command only tracks a single Str/Esc token. This is why the list-folding piece (TP3) is new, self-contained logic in resolve_dynamic_apply_lambda rather than something the existing constant-propagation lattice already half-does; it does not touch const_strings' storage, only reads it once per resolved element.

4. registry.command_prefixes() (tcl-registry/src/registry.rs:1169) is already the correct, generic, registry-driven primitive for 'this argument position names a command that will be invoked' (used today only by interprocedural.rs for IR-level call-graph reachability). Re-confirmed live against a fresh build (git status clean, binary newer than sources): `hover`/`definition` on `ActiveRecord find foo bar` in main2.tcl still return nothing; `Table find foo bar` in main.tcl is *also* currently broken (not explicitly retested by the original audit, but same root cause). tclsh9.0/8.6 both re-confirmed the oracle exactly as stated.

The stated root cause (receiver_instance_class gates bare receivers on instance_classes/created_instance_commands, which oo::class create never populates for the class's own bound command) is real and is exactly where the ooutil/ActiveRecord portion of the finding lives. BUT: while chasing the "stock TclOO self method" control case (native_check/native.tcl), I found the fix described in the hint is NOT sufficient to close that half of the finding. Using document-symbols, hover, completion and semantic-tokens on the live server I proved that `self method NAME {args} {body}` (and the `self { method ... }` block form) is a SEPARATE, more fundamental bug: rust/tcl-compiler/src/analyser/oo.rs's TclOO class-body walker (parse_oo_definition_body -> apply_oo_subcommand / collect_method_body) never unwraps the `self` wrapper member at all (only `private` has a handler, apply_oo_private) — so `class_def.class_methods` never gets an entry for a `self method`-declared member in the first place, and the method's body is never walked either (verified: a deliberately-wrong-arity `string length a b c d` inside a `private method` body — which shares the same wrapper gap — draws no diagnostic, while the identical call in a plain `method` body correctly draws E003 twice). Interestingly, `tcl-lsp-core/src/oo_body.rs` (the semantic-tokens/folding walker) already unwraps `self` correctly and generically (semantic-tokens confirms `make` is tagged `method [definition]`) — so the registry data (`MemberSpec::wrapper_or_body("self")` in tcl-registry/src/definer.rs) is right, only the tcl-compiler-side ClassDef-populating walker was never updated to consume it. tcl-compiler cannot depend on tcl-lsp-core (Cargo.toml confirms the dependency only goes the other way), so oo_body.rs's logic can't be reused as-is; oo.rs needs its own (small) fix mirroring its own existing `unwrap_wrapper_member` + `apply_oo_private` pattern.

I also found and empirically confirmed (via tclsh) a related precision requirement that a literal implementation of the hint would get wrong: ooutil's `classmethod` IS inherited by a subclass's own class-command (confirmed: Table find works because ooutil's Delegate-mixin machinery walks `info class superclass`, mirroring ClassDef.superclasses exactly), but a plain TclOO `self method` is NOT inherited by a subclass's own class-command (confirmed: Gadget, a plain `superclass Widget` subclass with no override, fails at runtime with "unknown method \"make\""). Reusing the existing MRO-walking `method_dispatch_definition` unmodified for the new class-command receiver would resolve `Gadget make` as if inherited -- a new, avoidable false positive. The fix therefore needs one bit of provenance on MethodDef so the class-command MRO walk can tell "declared via self" (class-local only) apart from "declared via classmethod / plain member" (inherited like an ordinary method) for ancestor providers, while still accepting either kind when the provider IS the receiver class itself.

Finally, references/rename's *whole-document* call-site enumeration (find_obj_method_call_sites in references.rs, reused by rename.rs) builds its receiver universe purely from analysis.instance_classes/created_instance_commands and early-returns when that's empty -- so even after receiver_instance_class is fixed (which only fixes single-cursor lookups: hover, go-to-def, prepare-rename), `references`/`rename` would still fail to find or rewrite the `ActiveRecord find` / `Table find` call sites, because nothing populates that separate scan's receiver set for a class's own name. This needs its own (small, precedent-mirroring) extension.

Net: this is a 3-part, 2-crate fix (tcl-compiler/src/analyser/oo.rs + tcl-lsp-core/src/definition.rs + tcl-lsp-core/src/references.rs), not the single-function fix the hint describes. All three reuse existing, established, already-tested helpers (unwrap_wrapper_member + apply_oo_private's shape; resolve_written_class_name, the exact function record_instance_creation's Pattern B already uses for the analogous "CLASS create NAME" case; and method_references_for_class's existing "walk inheriting subclasses too" precedent). No new registry infrastructure is needed; one new field on the existing MethodDef struct is needed for soundness.

The one addition: when calling method_dispatch_definition for the external-dispatch case (current line ~289), the caller needs to know whether `class_q` was reached via the NEW class-command path (pass MethodBucket::ClassOnly) or the existing instance path (MethodBucket::Both, or InstanceOnly if the companion fix lands). Cheapest way to know: re-check `analysis.instance_classes.contains_key(&inst)` (true => instance path) vs not (=> must be the new class-command path, since receiver_instance_class only returns Some via one of the two paths) right here, rather than changing receiver_instance_class's return type to carry a tag.

proposed_changes.description: Currently builds `var_set` purely from analysis.instance_classes (filtered to class_q or an inheriting-non-overriding subclass), early-returns `Vec::new()` when var_set is empty, then derives `cmd_set` as the subset of var_set names also in created_instance_commands. Fix: (1) move the early-return to after building the full cmd_set (see next point) so it no longer short-circuits before the class-command additions run; (2) after building cmd_set from var_set as today, also add: `let cq_is_class_level = analysis.all_classes.get(class_q).is_some_and(|cd| cd.class_methods.contains_key(method));` then if cq_is_class_level, insert class_q's own written forms (`cd.qualified_name.as_str()` and `cd.name.as_str()`, both borrowed from analysis.all_classes.get(class_q)) into cmd_set; additionally, only when the class_q-providing MethodDef has `is_self_method == false` (ooutil-classmethod-style, i.e. actually inherited), loop `for (other_q, other_cd) in &analysis.all_classes { if other_q != class_q && hierarchy.method_target(other_q, method) == Some(class_q) { cmd_set.insert(other_cd.qualified_name.as_str()); cmd_set.insert(other_cd.name.as_str()); } }` -- mirroring the exact inheriting-subclass loop already at the top of method_references_for_class (L536-542) for the intra-class `my method` body scan, just reading `other_cd`'s own name instead of its bodies. cmd_set already flows unchanged into the existing scan_obj_method_region/scan_obj_method_body machinery (matches by exact source-text equality against the bare head token, per L1124's `ctx.cmd_set.contains(raw)` -- this is why both the qualified and simple written forms need to be inserted, covering `ActiveRecord find` and `::ActiveRecord find` as written).
proposed_changes.existing_pattern_to_reuse: method_references_for_class's own inheriting-subclass loop (references.rs L535-542, immediately above where find_obj_method_call_sites is called) is the direct precedent -- same hierarchy.method_target(...) == Some(class_q) test, just contributing a name to a receiver set instead of a body span to a scan list.

test_scenarios.description: main2.tcl-shape: `oo::class create ActiveRecord { classmethod find args { puts "[self] called with arguments: $args" } }` then a later top-level `ActiveRecord find foo bar`. Go-to-definition with the cursor on `find` in the call must return exactly one location: the `find` in `classmethod find args {...}`. Requires only Part 2 (ooutil's classmethod idiom is already correctly extracted into class_methods today).

Same file, `oo::class create Table { superclass ActiveRecord }` then `Table find foo bar`. Go-to-definition on `find` in that call must resolve to ActiveRecord's `classmethod find` declaration (inherited via the ordinary superclass MRO walk). Requires Part 2 with is_self_method==false accepted from an ancestor provider (or absent the refinement, this case works even with the naive fix -- it's the one the hint explicitly anticipated).

`oo::class create Widget { self method make {n} { return "made $n" } }` then `puts [Widget make gadget]`. Go-to-definition/hover on `make` in the call must resolve to the `make` in `self method make {n} {...}`. Requires BOTH Part 1 (self recognized at all) and Part 2 (receiver resolution).

Same Widget source: hover directly on `make` at its OWN declaration site (inside `self method make {n} { ... }`) must now show a classmethod-style hover (e.g. "**classmethod** `::Widget::make` (1 param(s))"), and `symbols`/`completion` after `Widget ` must list `make`. This isolates and proves Part 1 alone, independent of the call-site receiver bug.

From main2.tcl's `Table` declaration span (any of Table's methods) or from either call site, `references` on `find` must enumerate: the declaration in `classmethod find args {...}`, the `Table find foo bar` call, and the `ActiveRecord find foo bar` call (three ranges total, no duplicates). Requires Part 3 in addition to Part 2 (Part 2 alone only fixes single-cursor lookups, not the whole-document scan references relies on).

`rename` invoked with the cursor on `find` inside `ActiveRecord find foo bar` (the call site, not the declaration), renaming to `lookup`. Resulting edits must rewrite: the declaration (`classmethod find` -> `classmethod lookup`), the `Table find` call, and the `ActiveRecord find` call -- three edits, none missed. Requires Part 2 (to resolve which method the cursor targets) + Part 3 (to enumerate every site to rewrite, since rename.rs's rename_method_in_class/rename_method both delegate to references::method_references_for_class).

`oo::class create Widget { self method make {n} {...} } }` then `oo::class create Gadget { superclass Widget }` (no override) then `Gadget make foo`. Go-to-definition/hover on `make` in that call must return NOTHING (0 locations), matching real Tcl (`unknown method "make": must be create, destroy or new`, confirmed via tclsh9.0/8.6). This is the critical precision test for the is_self_method refinement in Part 1+2 -- without it, a naive reuse of the existing MRO walk WOULD incorrectly resolve this to Widget's declaration (confirmed by hand-tracing the unmodified method_dispatch_definition against Gadget's MRO, which does include Widget).

`oo::class create ActiveRecord { classmethod find args {...} }` then `ActiveRecord create rec1` then `rec1 find foo bar` (an actual instance calling a classmethod). Go-to-definition on `find` here should ideally return nothing (real Tcl: `unknown method "find": must be <cloned>, create, ...`) -- but this is the PRE-EXISTING bug (secondary issue 3), already reproducing today before any of these changes land, not a new regression risk from Parts 1-3 themselves. Include this as a documented xfail/known-limitation test if the companion fix (tightening the two existing method_dispatch_definition call sites) is deferred, or as a real TN if it's bundled in.

`set d [ActiveRecord new]; d find foo bar` (bare `d`, no `$`, `d` is a plain variable never bound as a command). Go-to-definition on `find` must stay 0 locations -- `d` is not itself a class name (resolve_written_class_name("d", ...) fails) and is not a created-instance-command, so neither branch of the extended receiver_instance_class fires. Regression guard mirroring the existing definition_bare_var_receiver_without_dollar_does_not_resolve test, now exercised alongside the new class-command branch to make sure the new branch doesn't accidentally widen this case.

`oo::class create Base { classmethod find args {...} }` then `oo::class create UsesMixin { mixin Base }` (mixin, not superclass) then `UsesMixin find foo bar`. Real Tcl (confirmed via tclsh) rejects this at runtime (`unknown method "find"`) because ooutil's Delegate propagation only follows `superclass`, not `mixin`. If the implementer reuses the full mixin-inclusive mro_map as-is (the simplest option, explicitly recommended above with a documented caveat), this WILL incorrectly resolve -- include this as an explicit, currently-accepted-limitation test (marked xfail / documented in a code comment) rather than silently letting it regress unnoticed; only turn it into a true TN if the implementer adds a superclass-only linearization.

`oo::class create Widget { self { method make {n} { return "made $n" } } }` (the `self { ... }` block form rather than the prefix form) then `Widget make gadget`. Confirmed via tclsh this is valid and behaves identically to the prefix form; confirmed via the live server that it is ALSO currently unresolved (symbols shows 0 methods for this shape too). Part 1 as scoped above (prefix form only) will NOT fix this -- document as a known, pre-existing (private has the same gap), lower-priority follow-up rather than silently leaving it unmentioned in the PR.

Should the companion fix in method_dispatch_definition / obj_method_hover_text (tightening the two EXISTING instance-dispatch call sites to methods-only, closing the confirmed `rec1 find` false positive) be bundled into this same patch, or filed as its own follow-up? I did not compile any of this (research-only, no file edits per instructions) -- the unwrap_wrapper_member index-shifting arithmetic in the collect_method_body change was verified by hand-tracing both the wrapper and non-wrapper cases against METHOD_ROLES' exact (0,Name)/(1,ParamList)/(2,Body) layout, and I'm confident in it, but it's the one piece of this plan I'd most want to see through `cargo test -p tcl-compiler` (the existing oo.rs unit tests -- method_subcommand_records_method_def, classmethod_subcommand_records_class_method, private_method_records_with_private_visibility, etc. -- should all still pass unchanged if the refactor is algebraically equivalent as designed) before considering Part 1 done.
